target: Glume (PO:0009039) absent (PATO:0000462) only in the male spikelets (spikelet PO:0009051, context 'male' / 'staminate'). The female spikelets have glumes, thinner than the fertile lemma (PO:0009037)
fix: 'Male spikelet glumes absent', 'female florets without lemma' and similar phrases with a sex word in front of the part apply only to that sex. Keep 'male' or 'female' as the context and never record a taxon-wide absence.
reason: Olyra is monoecious, and its male spikelets lack glumes. The glume compared with the fertile lemma belongs to the female spikelet.

target: Lower glume (PO:0006002) present, with no lateral veins (1-veined). Only the lateral veins are absent. The glume itself is present and obtuse
fix: '<part> <subpart> absent' ('lower glume lateral veins absent', 'lemma awns absent') denies the last noun, the subpart. Never record an absence of the head part, and never fall back from 'lower glume' to glume PO:0009039.
reason: The sentence is about the veins of the lower glume. A glume without veins cannot be obtuse and absent at once.

target: Lemma (PO:0009037) present and not keeled, i.e. rounded on the back. Nothing is absent. Do not use keel PO:0025327 (the papilionaceous petals) or keel-shaped PATO:0002522
fix: 'without keel', 'not keeled' and 'ecarinate' said of a glume, lemma, sepal or leaf describe the shape of that organ (no ridge on the back). They are never an absence of the organ, and never PO keel PO:0025327.
reason: A keel on a grass lemma is a ridge, not a separate part. The indurate lemma is present.

target: Glumes (upper glume PO:0006004) present and not keeled. Nothing is absent. The upper glume is elliptic
fix: Same rule as for the lemma: 'without keels' on a glume or lemma is a shape (back rounded, no ridge). Never record it as glume absent or as PO keel PO:0025327.
reason: Paspalum has an upper glume, and here it is described as elliptic. 'Without keels' only describes the shape of its back.

target: Stipel (PO:0020051) absent (PATO:0000462). Stipules (PO:0020041) are present and caducous
fix: 'stipels' and 'stipellae' map to stipel PO:0020051, never to stipule PO:0020041. Do not lemmatise or fuzzy-match 'stipel' to 'stipule'.
reason: Stipels (on the leaflets) and stipules (at the leaf base) are different organs. Dalbergia has caducous stipules and no stipels.

target: Trichome (PO:0000282) absent on the leaf (context: leaf PO:0025034). The leaf is present. The second statement ('present on abaxial and adaxial surfaces') belongs to another character of the leaf, such as stomata or scales, not to the leaf itself
fix: In 'Character: value' lists (Smithsonian, DELTA-style), 'Hairs: absent' denies the named character (trichome PO:0000282) on the organ of the section heading. The heading organ is only the context. 'present on <surfaces>' attaches to the character named in its own line.
reason: The leaf section lists hairs and other surface features. Neither line says anything about whether leaves are present.

target: Cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. The stem is a leafless scape. The basal leaves (rosette leaf PO:0000014) are present and waxy
fix: 'leafless stem', 'leafless scape' and 'scapose' deny the cauline leaves only. Map them to cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent, never to leaf PO:0025034 absent.
reason: Camassia has basal leaves and a leafless flowering stem. The waxy leaves are the basal ones.

target: Only the allomorphic pistillate flowers are absent: pistillate flower (PO:0025599) with 'allomorphic' as context. The normal staminate, pistillate and bisexual flowers are present
fix: 'allomorphic pistillate flowers absent' (Acalypha) denies only that special form. Keep 'allomorphic' as the context and never record 'flower absent' or 'pistillate flower absent'.
reason: The same description lists staminate, pistillate and bisexual flowers in terminal inflorescences. Only the special allomorphic form is missing.

target: Only the annulus (the thickened ring at the mouth of the perianth tube) is absent. Perianth (PO:0009058) present, with 'annulus' as the context. In Aristolochia the perianth is a calyx, and corolla PO:0009059 should not be used at all
fix: In Aristolochiaceae, 'annulus absent' and 'syrinx absent' deny a ring or throat structure of the perianth tube. Record them as perianth with that context, never as corolla absent. Aristolochia perianth statements map to perianth PO:0009058, not to corolla.
reason: An absent annulus does not remove the perianth, which is described as glabrous. Aristolochia has no corolla.

target: Only the syrinx (the ring-like collar in the perianth throat) is absent. Perianth (PO:0009058) present, with 'syrinx' as the context. 'Tube upright' is the perianth tube: perianth with 'tube' as the context, erect. Not corolla
fix: Same rule as for 'annulus absent': in Aristolochia, 'syrinx absent' denies only that structure of the perianth, never the corolla or the perianth.
reason: The perianth tube is described as upright, so the perianth is present. Only the throat collar is missing.

target: Colleter (FLOPO:0986023) absent on the leaf lamina (context: leaf lamina PO:0020039). The lamina is present and membranous
fix: 'laminar colleters absent', 'petiolar glands absent' and similar phrases deny the gland-like part named by the noun. The adjective gives its position (lamina, petiole). Map them to colleter FLOPO:0986023 absent, with the organ as context.
reason: 'Laminar' says where the colleters would be. Asclepias leaves have blades.

target: The basal bladeless sheaths are cataphylls: scale leaf (PO:0006003), or leaf sheath (PO:0020104) with 'basal, bladeless' as the context. The foliage leaves have glabrous blades (leaf lamina PO:0020039)
fix: 'bladeless', 'bladeless sheaths' and 'basal sheaths bladeless' in Cyperaceae, Poaceae and Juncaceae refer to the basal cataphylls. Map them to scale leaf PO:0006003 and never to 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Carex houghtoniana has leaf blades. Only the lowest sheaths have none (the same case as the example in docs/km-classification.md).

target: 'branches not twisted' describes the inflorescence branches (inflorescence PO:0009049, with 'branch' as the context) and is a negation: not twisted, not 'torsioned'. Axillary vegetative branches (branch PO:0025073, context 'axillary') stay absent
fix: In Crassulaceae, 'branches' inside the inflorescence paragraph means the cyme branches, not shoot branches. 'not twisted' and 'not <quality>' must keep the negation and never be recorded as the positive quality.
reason: The plant lacks axillary shoot branches but has branched cymes. The present statement both names the wrong part and drops the 'not'.

target: Only basal (axillary, hidden) spikelets are absent: spikelet (PO:0009051) with 'basal' as the context. The terminal spikelet is present
fix: 'basal spikelets absent', 'basal flowers absent' and 'axillary inflorescences absent' deny only the parts at that position. Keep the position as the context and never record a taxon-wide absence.
reason: Eleocharis has a single terminal spikelet. Some species also have hidden basal spikelets, and this species lacks them. 'Terete' may describe the culm rather than the spikelet.

target: The caudex, the woody perennial stem base, is absent. The stem (PO:0009047) is present and solid. Record the absence as stem with 'caudex' as the context, or not at all, until there is a caudex class
fix: 'caudex' is a synonym of stem PO:0009047 in the lexicon. 'caudex absent' or 'without a caudex' must not resolve through that synonym to 'stem absent'. Keep 'caudex' as the context, or block absences of synonyms that name only a region of the stem.
reason: A plant without a caudex still has flowering stems, which are described here. The synonym turned the absence of a stem base into the absence of every stem.

target: Cauline leaf (PO:0000013) absent. The basal leaves (rosette leaf PO:0000014) are present and ± sessile
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' and 'stem leaves 0' map to cauline leaf PO:0000013. Never drop 'cauline'.
reason: Lewisia kelloggii is a rosette plant. The sessile leaves are the basal ones.

target: Seed (PO:0009010) present and dark-mottled. Only the recurved flap over the hilum is absent: hilum (PO:0020063) with 'recurved flap' as the context
fix: '<structure> over/on <part> absent' denies the first-named structure. The rest of the phrase gives its position. Never record an absence of the head organ (seed) of the section.
reason: The seeds are described, so only the small flap near the hilum is missing.

target: Only the outer (petaloid) stamens are without anthers. They are staminodes (PO:0009077), or stamens with 'outer' as the context. The inner stamens have anthers (PO:0009066), which are straight after dehiscence
fix: 'outer stamens petaloid, without anthers', 'staminodes without anthers' and 'sterile stamens lacking anthers' deny anthers only in those members. Record staminode PO:0009077 present, or keep 'outer' as the context. Never record 'anther absent'.
reason: Mentzelia has petaloid outer staminodes without anthers. The fertile stamens are described with anthers.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent only on the peduncle (PO:0009053, as context), or no calyculus (epicalyx PO:0009063). The phyllaries (involucral bract PO:0009045) are present, and the inner ones are lanceolate
fix: In Asteraceae, 'ebracteate' said of peduncles or scapes means no bracts on that stalk, or no calyculus. It never denies the involucral bracts (phyllaries), so never record 'bract absent' for a head.
reason: Every Microseris head has phyllaries. 'Ebracteate' refers to the stalk below the head.

target: Only the axillary leaf fascicles are absent: leaf (PO:0025034) with 'axillary' as the context. The main leaves are present. Their margins are NOT thickened, so the 'increased thickness' annotation is also wrong
fix: 'axillary leaves absent' and 'axillary fascicles absent' (Caryophyllaceae) deny only the secondary leaves in the leaf axils. Keep 'axillary' as the context. 'not thickened' must keep its negation.
reason: Minuartia drummondii has opposite leaves. Only the extra axillary tufts are missing. The present statement also lost its 'not'.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) absent only on the peduncle (PO:0009053, as context). The phyllaries (involucral bract PO:0009045) are present. The rounded apices are probably those of the leaves or phyllaries, not of peduncle bracts
fix: 'Peduncles ebracteate' and 'peduncle without bracteoles' keep 'peduncle' as the context and never become 'bract absent'. A following 'apices rounded' attaches to the organ of its own sentence, never to bracts that were just denied.
reason: Packera heads have phyllaries. Only the peduncle is bare, so the two statements are about different bracts.

target: Phyllode leaf (PO:0025335) absent: the flat, non-pitcher winter leaves are missing. The pitcher leaves (vascular leaf PO:0009025, synonym 'pitcher') are present, and the rim is maroon
fix: 'phyllodia absent' and 'phyllodes absent' map to phyllode leaf PO:0025335 and never fall back to leaf PO:0025034. In Sarracenia, 'rim', 'hood' and 'tube' belong to the pitcher leaf.
reason: Sarracenia jonesii has pitchers but no flat phyllodes. The maroon rim belongs to the pitcher.

target: Sterile bracts on the peduncle (bract PO:0009055 with 'peduncle' PO:0009053 as the context) are absent. The floral bracts are present and much shorter than the ovary
fix: In Orchidaceae, 'peduncle ebracteate' or 'scape without sterile bracts' denies only the bracts on the stalk below the flowers. Keep 'peduncle' as the context. The floral bracts stay present.
reason: Each orchid flower has a floral bract. Only the peduncle is bare.

target: Only the inner petals are absent or vestigial: petal (PO:0009032) with 'inner whorl' as the context. The outer petals are present and glabrous inside
fix: 'inner petals absent', 'inner whorl absent' and 'outer sepals absent' deny one whorl only. Keep 'inner' or 'outer' as the context and never record 'petal absent'.
reason: Annona reticulata has three outer petals, and its inner petals are absent or minute. The glabrous petals are the outer ones.

target: Awn (PO:0025349) absent on one floret or spikelet (lower lemma, or the pedicelled spikelet). It is present on the other (upper lemma of the sessile spikelet). Keep the floret or spikelet as the context
fix: In Poaceae descriptions, 'awnless' and 'awned' in the same treatment refer to different florets, lemmas or spikelets (lower/upper, sessile/pedicelled). Attach each to the floret or spikelet of its own clause and never record a taxon-wide awn absence.
reason: Apocopis has an awned upper lemma and awnless lower parts. The two words describe different members.

target: Leaf lamina intramarginal vein (PO:0025520) absent. The leaf lamina (PO:0020039) is present and membranous
fix: 'marginal vein absent', 'intramarginal vein absent' and 'collecting vein absent' map to leaf lamina intramarginal vein PO:0025520. Never fall back to leaf lamina absent.
reason: Myrsinaceae descriptions note whether a marginal collecting vein is present. The blade is clearly present.

target: The basal bladeless sheaths are cataphylls: scale leaf (PO:0006003). The foliage leaf blades (leaf lamina PO:0020039) are present and flat
fix: 'bladeless sheaths' map to scale leaf PO:0006003, or to leaf sheath PO:0020104 with 'bladeless' as the context. Never record 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: The exact pattern named in docs/km-classification.md. The Carex leaves have flat blades.

target: Inflorescence bract (bract PO:0009055) inconspicuous or not leaf-like, i.e. reduced. Nothing is absent. The glumes (PO:0009039) are papery
fix: 'without distinct <part>', 'without conspicuous <part>' and 'not leaf-like' describe a reduced or inconspicuous part, never an absence. Map them to a size or shape quality, or drop them.
reason: 'Without distinct involucral bract leaf' says that the lowest bract does not look like a leaf. The bract is still there.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) present, without a sheath (sheathless). Only the bract sheath is absent. The male glumes (PO:0009039) are yellowish white
fix: 'bracts without sheaths', 'sheathless' and 'esheathing' deny the sheath of the bract (in Carex keys), never the bract. Record bract with 'sheath' as the context, absent.
reason: In Carex, bracts are described as sheathing or sheathless. Here the bract is present and only its sheath is missing.

target: Rosette leaf (PO:0000014), or leaf with 'basal' as the context, absent. The cauline leaves (PO:0000013) are present and papillose at the axil
fix: 'basal leaves absent' maps to rosette leaf PO:0000014, or to leaf with 'basal' as the context. Never drop 'basal' (same rule as the earlier reviewed items).
reason: Chrysosplenium giraldianum lacks basal leaves but has stem leaves. The papillose axils belong to the stem leaves.
